topics.name: Versatile carbon: homologous series, isomers, functional groups

questions.title: The odd pair in a homologous series
questions.text: Which of the following sets of compounds does not belong to the same homologous series?
steps: ① Same series ⟹ same general formula
② Alkanes: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ (CH₄, C₂H₆, C₃H₈, C₄H₁₀, C₅H₁₂)
③ (a), (b), (c): every member fits CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ ✓
④ C₄H₈ fits CₙH₂ₙ: an alkene
⑤ C₅H₁₂ is an alkane ⟹ different series
questions.remember: Homologous series: same functional group and general formula; successive members differ by –CH₂– (14 u). Alkanes CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, alkenes CₙH₂ₙ, alkynes CₙH₂ₙ₋₂.
questions.trap: Thinking members must be 'next to each other'. CH₄ and C₄H₁₀ are both alkanes, so they ARE in the same series.
questions.tryit: Which series does C₃H₄ belong to?

questions.title: Inside a soap micelle
questions.text: While washing dirty clothes with soap, micelles are formed. Select the correct statement about micelles.
opts: The hydrophobic tail of the soap molecule is in the interior of the cluster, whereas the hydrophilic end is on the surface.
The hydrophobic tail is on the surface of the cluster, whereas the hydrophilic end is in the interior.
Both the hydrophobic tail and the hydrophilic end are in the interior of the cluster.
Both the hydrophobic tail and the hydrophilic end are on the surface of the cluster.
steps: ① Soap molecule: long hydrocarbon tail + ionic head
② Tail hates water (hydrophobic), loves oil
③ Head loves water (hydrophilic)
④ Tails dig into the oil drop, heads face the water
⑤ The cluster (micelle) washes away with water
∴ Tail inside, head on the surface → (a)
questions.ans: Option (a) Hydrophobic tail inside, hydrophilic end on the surface
questions.remember: Soap: ionic (hydrophilic) head + long hydrocarbon (hydrophobic) tail. In water the tails point into the oil, heads outward: a micelle.
questions.trap: Picking (b): it reverses the roles. The WATER-loving head must face the water outside.
questions.ncert: NCERT Ch 4 · Section 4.5 Soaps and detergents
questions.tryit: Why don't soaps lather well in hard water?
questions.tryans: Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺ ions react with soap to form an insoluble scum

questions.title: Butane and its twin
questions.text:
Consider the structures X and Y:
X: CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–CH₃ (a straight chain of four carbons)
Y: CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH₃ (three carbons in a chain with one branch)
Which statements are correct?
(i) X and Y are homologues.
(ii) X and Y have the same structural formula, but different molecular formula.
(iii) X and Y have the same molecular formula, but different structural formula.
(iv) X and Y are structural isomers.
steps: ① Count X: 4 C, 10 H ⟹ C₄H₁₀
② Count Y: 4 C, 10 H ⟹ C₄H₁₀
③ Same molecular formula, different arrangement ⟹ (iii) ✓
④ That is the definition of structural isomers ⟹ (iv) ✓
⑤ Homologues differ by CH₂ ⟹ (i) ✗; (ii) ✗
∴ (iii) and (iv) → (d)
questions.remember: Structural isomers: same molecular formula, different structures (butane and isobutane are both C₄H₁₀). Homologues differ by –CH₂–.
questions.trap: Picking (i): homologues have DIFFERENT molecular formulas (they differ by CH₂). These two have the same.
questions.ncert: NCERT Ch 4 · Section 4.2.2 (structural isomers of butane)
questions.tryit: How many structural isomers does pentane (C₅H₁₂) have?

questions.title: Which solutions light the bulb?
questions.text: Four solutions, namely fructose, ethanol, hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide, are taken in four separate beakers and connected one by one in an electric circuit with a bulb. The solutions in which the bulb will glow are:
steps: ① Current flows only if the solution has ions
② HCl in water → H⁺ + Cl⁻ ✓
③ NaOH in water → Na⁺ + OH⁻ ✓
④ Fructose and ethanol: covalent, no ions ✗
∴ HCl and NaOH → (d)
questions.ans: Option (d) hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide
questions.remember: Acids and bases give ions in water, so their solutions conduct. Covalent compounds like glucose, fructose and ethanol don't form ions.
questions.trap: Picking ethanol because it's a liquid 'like water'. It's covalent: no ions, no current.
questions.ncert: NCERT Ch 2 · Activity 2.8 and Ch 4 · Section 4.1
questions.tryit: Why doesn't distilled water conduct well?

questions.title: Assertion–Reason: glacial acetic acid
questions.text:
Assertion (A): Pure ethanoic acid is also known as glacial acetic acid.
Reason (R): Pure ethanoic acid often freezes during winter due to its low melting point of 290 K.
opts: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
steps: ① Ethanoic acid = acetic acid, CH₃COOH
② Pure acid melts at 290 K (about 17 °C) ✓ R true
③ Below 290 K, in cold winters, it freezes like ice
④ That ice-like look gave it the name glacial ✓ A true
⑤ R gives the reason for the name in A
∴ Answer: (a)
questions.remember: Pure ethanoic acid melts at 290 K, so it freezes in cold weather: 'glacial' acetic acid. Vinegar is a 5–8% solution of it.
questions.trap: Thinking 290 K is 'high'. 290 K is about 17 °C: room temperature in winter is easily below it.
questions.ncert: NCERT Ch 4 · Section 4.4.2 Properties of ethanoic acid
questions.tryans: A 5–8% solution of ethanoic acid in water

questions.title: Identify P: ethanol and its reactions (5 marks)
questions.text:
A carbon compound P of molecular formula C₂H₆O is neutral to red and blue litmus. A gas that burns with a pop sound is produced when sodium reacts with P.
(i) Identify the compound P.
(ii) P is heated with conc. H₂SO₄ at 443 K to produce compound Q. (I) Write the chemical equation. (II) What is the role of conc. H₂SO₄?
(iii) What is observed on heating P with ethanoic acid with an acid as a catalyst? Write the chemical equation.
steps: ① C₂H₆O, neutral, gives H₂ with Na ⟹ P = ethanol, C₂H₅OH
② 2C₂H₅OH + 2Na → 2C₂H₅ONa + H₂ (pop test)
③ (ii) C₂H₅OH → CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O (conc. H₂SO₄, 443 K) ⟹ Q = ethene
④ Role of conc. H₂SO₄: dehydrating agent (removes water)
⑤ (iii) CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH → CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O (acid)
⑥ A sweet-smelling ester forms: esterification
∴ Ethanol · ethene, dehydrating agent · sweet ester
questions.ans: (i) P = ethanol, C₂H₅OH · (ii) C₂H₅OH → CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O; conc. H₂SO₄ is a dehydrating agent · (iii) a sweet-smelling ester: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH → CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O
questions.remember: Ethanol + Na → H₂; ethanol + hot conc. H₂SO₄ (443 K) → ethene (dehydration); ethanol + ethanoic acid (acid catalyst) → ester (esterification).
questions.trap: Saying P is an acid because it reacts with sodium. It's NEUTRAL to litmus: alcohols also give H₂ with Na.
questions.tryit: What happens when the ester is heated with NaOH?
questions.tryans: Saponification: it gives back ethanol and sodium ethanoate

questions.title: Carbon's puzzle, homologues and oxidation (5 marks)
questions.text:
(i) Carbon cannot form C⁴⁺ cation and C⁴⁻ anion. Explain.
(ii) Define homologous series of carbon compounds. Why are the melting and boiling points of C₄H₁₀ higher than C₃H₈ or C₂H₆?
(iii) What happens when ethanol is heated with acidified potassium dichromate?
steps: ① C⁴⁺: losing 4 electrons needs too much energy
② C⁴⁻: 6 protons can't hold 10 electrons ⟹ so carbon SHARES electrons (covalent)
③ Homologous series: same functional group, members differ by –CH₂–
④ Bigger molecule ⟹ higher mass ⟹ stronger attractions ⟹ higher m.p., b.p.
⑤ (iii) CH₃CH₂OH → CH₃COOH (acidified K₂Cr₂O₇, heat)
⑥ Ethanol is oxidised to ethanoic acid; orange → green
∴ Shares electrons · –CH₂– steps · ethanoic acid
questions.ans: (i) C⁴⁺ needs too much energy; C⁴⁻ can't be held by 6 protons, so carbon shares electrons · (ii) same functional group, successive members differ by –CH₂–; larger molecules have higher mass and stronger forces · (iii) ethanol is oxidised to ethanoic acid
questions.remember: Carbon has 4 valence electrons: it forms covalent bonds by sharing. Acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ or alkaline KMnO₄ (heat) oxidise ethanol to ethanoic acid.
questions.trap: Writing 'the C–C bond is weak'. Carbon forms covalent bonds because ionic C⁴⁺/C⁴⁻ are energetically impossible, and the C–C bond is strong.
questions.tryit: What colour change shows that ethanol has been oxidised by acidified K₂Cr₂O₇?
